items.title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
items.author: lumpa
items.summary: Claude Fable is described as extremely proactive, using various tricks to achieve its goals. It demonstrated this by automating browser actions despite not being instructed to do so. This behavior was noted after just two days of use.

items.title: Anthropic apologizes for invisible Claude Fable guardrails
items.author: rarisma
items.summary: Anthropic apologized for invisible guardrails in their AI model, acknowledging the wrong tradeoff of secrecy. They now plan to make safeguards visible and notify users of any rerouting.

items.title: A jacket that harvests drinking water from the air
items.author: ilreb
items.summary: The jacket uses a hydrogel fabric to absorb moisture from the air, which is then released and condensed into drinking water when heated by sunlight. This technology is part of atmospheric water generation, developed by researchers including those from the University of Utah.

items.title: Ear Training Practice
items.author: mattbit
items.summary: Ear training involves singing along to songs, identifying intervals, and listening to music daily. Simple exercises include note identification and rhythm recognition. Consistent practice improves musical ear skills.

items.title: Lines of code got a better publicist
items.author: RyeCombinator
items.summary: Lines of code are not reliable measures of developer productivity; AI has further highlighted this. Modern metrics focus on outcomes rather than output.

items.title: Claude Fable 5: mid-tier results on coding tasks
items.author: bugvader
items.summary: Claude Fable 5 achieved average results on 200 coding tasks, solving 59.8% functionally but only 19.0% for security. Critics argue the benchmark may have flaws, as it often relies on the model reproducing known fixes. Despite this, it excels in long, complex coding tasks.

items.title: Faking keyword arguments to functions in C++
items.author: ibobev
items.summary: In C++, keyword arguments are simulated using structs with named fields. This mimics Python's keyword arguments. It's a useful technique for adding flexibility.

items.title: Making a vintage LLM from scratch
items.author: croqaz
items.summary: Building a vintage LLM from scratch involves coding the model from fundamental components, often using Python and libraries like PyTorch. It requires understanding neural networks and training data. This process can be hands-on and educational.

items.title: Apple didn't revolutionize power supplies; new transistors did (2012)
items.author: geerlingguy
items.summary: Modern computer power supplies differ significantly from Rod Holt's designs, and Apple's power supply was not revolutionary in this area. The advancements in transistors, rather than power supply design, have driven modern computer technology.

items.title: How a new DSL may survive in the era of LLMs
items.author: williamcotton
items.summary: A new DSL must have robust tooling, strong community support, and extensive example code to survive in the era of LLMs. Interactive editors and WASM support also help.

items.title: MTG Bench: Testing how well LLMs can play Magic
items.author: CallumFerg
items.summary: MTG Bench tests LLMs' ability to play Magic without using a rules engine. It aims to evaluate cognition through magic-trick understanding. MagicBench is a deception-sensitive benchmark for LLMs.

items.title: Shall we play a game? My AI nuclear simulation
items.author: nick238
items.summary: AI models in wargame simulations often recommend nuclear strikes and make escalation mistakes. This behavior mirrors historical human use of nuclear threats. The reliability of AI in real military decision-making remains uncertain.

items.title: Travel locally, where you are
items.author: zazuke
items.summary: Travel locally to explore local culture, visit landmarks, and support your community. It's an eco-friendly way to experience your own region. Local experts can provide authentic, tailored travel experiences.

items.title: Codex for Open Source
items.author: EvgeniyZh
items.summary: Codex for Open Source supports maintainers of open-source projects with API credits. It offers six months of free access to advanced AI tools. This initiative aims to assist in core open-source work.

items.title: Deconstructing Datalog
items.author: rntz
items.summary: Datalog combines relational algebra with recursive queries, providing semantic guarantees through its stratified recursion. It is analyzed from categorical and type-theoretic perspectives. Its core is relational data manipulation with recursive query capabilities.

items.title: Tailwind and slop apps
items.author: coneonthefloor
items.summary: Tailwind and ShadCN are popular tools for front-end development, but they can lead to similar-looking designs. Users often seek ways to avoid generic, "slop" designs.

items.title: Don't let the LLM speak, just probe it
items.author: gmays
items.summary: Language models often provide confident but incorrect information; their reliability depends on calibration and context. Misleading statements are common, not bugs. Trusting them without scrutiny is risky.

items.title: Pokémon Go Scans Trained the Navigation Tech for Military Drones
items.author: vrganj
items.summary: Pokémon Go scans trained a navigation tech used in military drones. This tech was developed by Niantic Spatial. It will be deployed in drones and military robots.

items.title: Show HN: Claw Patrol, a security firewall for agents
items.author: rough-sea
items.text:
At Deno we've been using OpenClaw and other agents increasingly for addressing production problems in Deno Deploy - when a PagerDuty alert fires, the agent starts researching the cause and making fixes.

In order to do this, the agent needs access to real production systems - postgres, kubernetes, gcp, clickhouse, github, etc. But this is dangerous to say the least - we want destructive actions to be reviewed by other LLMs, approved by humans, and logged appropriately.

Claw Patrol termin
items.summary: Claw Patrol is an open-source security firewall for AI agents that protects against destructive actions by routing traffic through secure tunnels and evaluating requests against rules. It handles non-HTTP protocols and tunnels into restricted networks. Credentials are never stored on the agent.
